answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through capacity-bounded trust graphs. Nodes route credit only across edges verified by prior collaboration, like co-evaluating a structured sonnet. A periodic consensus pulse recalculates graph bottlenecks, forcing an attacker to spend scarce relational capital and interaction time per identity. However, this balances the system on a narrow ledge between security and stagnation, as honest newcomers struggle to obtain initial endorsements.
